The story takes place in the small village of Hinamizawa, where the protagonist, Keiichi Maebara, moves to in June of 1983. He quickly befriends a group of classmates, including Mion Sonozaki, her twin sister Shion, Rena Ryūgū, Rika Furude, and Satoko Hōjō. Hinamizawa is initially peaceful, and the village is preparing for the annual Watanagashi Festival, which is dedicated to the local deity Oyashiro.

However, Keiichi soon learns that for the past four years, murders and disappearances have been occurring on the day of the festival, leading to rumors of an "Oyashiro Curse" among the villagers. In the latest incident, a freelance photographer named Jirō Tomitake is found dead with his throat torn out, and the village nurse, Miyo Takano, is found charred in the village clinic.

The story progresses through different arcs, each with different perspectives and outcomes. In most arcs, Keiichi or one of his friends attempts to investigate the mysteries of Hinamizawa and the Oyashiro Curse, only to succumb to paranoia and homicidal rage. In some arcs, Rika's body is found in the family shrine, while others end with the cataclysmic destruction of the village, explained as a release of swamp gas.

The answer arcs reveal that each preceding arc is an alternate reality in which Rika tried and failed to save herself and her friends. As a priestess of the Furude Shrine, Rika can communicate with the spirit Hanyū, who served as the basis for Oyashiro and is the ancestress of the Furude clan. Each time Rika died, Hanyū would move her to another reality, but Rika never retains the memory of how she died, making it difficult for her to prevent it.

In the final two chapters, it is revealed that the village clinic is secretly a government institute investigating Hinamizawa Syndrome, a disease that induces paranoia, delusion, and homicidal rage in its victims before pushing them to tear out their own throats. The women of the Furude clan have all acted as Infection Queens, and Rika is the sole remaining member of the line after the death of her parents in the 1981 incident.

Miyo Takano's adoptive grandfather, Hifumi Takano, believes that if there is no Infection Queen, all villagers will succumb to the syndrome, and a mass outbreak of violence will occur. In some of the realities, Shion, succumbing to Hinamizawa Syndrome, kills Rika; however, life in Hinamizawa goes on, showing that Hifumi's theories have been exaggerated. In most of the realities, Miyo kills Rika, and the threat of the mass outbreak convinces the government to massacre the village, with the release of swamp gas being a cover story.

After several hundred loops, Keiichi becomes either vividly or subconsciously aware of the previous realities, allowing him to avoid critical points where various characters would be murdered or driven insane. In the final loop, the group asks Hanyū to join them, and the spirit manages to manifest a physical body. With her assistance and all of the knowledge and allies they have formed along the way, they thwart Miyo's plan and go on to live happy lives afterward.

The story of "When They Cry" is a complex and deeply disturbing tale that explores themes of violence, trauma, and the cyclical nature of history, ultimately leading to a hopeful and satisfying conclusion.
